messages.subject: Planting
messages.text:
Will it be too late for me to plant the bombs now that it is almost July? If so, can I refrigerate them until the Fall of next Spring? 

 Thanks
 Stan

messages.subject: Re: Planting
messages.text:
It's not too late to plant now, but if you decide to wait, refrigerating them until next spring is also a safe option if they haven't sprouted when you receive them!
 

 Another option is to plant them in large pots, make sure they have enough light, and then transplant them next spring 😊
 

 Warmly,
 __
 Gabriel 
 Co-founder 
 Lasclay

messages.subject: Re: Planting
messages.text:
Hello Stan,
 We hope you’re doing well.
 

 We’re truly sorry to hear that your milkweed seed bombs didn’t germinate as expected. We know how exciting it is to start growing and how disappointing this can be.
 

 After careful review, we’ve identified that the issue may be linked to the shipping process, which can sometimes affect seed viability. The good news is: we’ve taken action.
 

 We’ve now introduced cold-stratified milkweed seeds, ready to plant , specifically designed to give you a much higher success rate from the very first try.
 

 While our policy does not allow refunds or exchanges on seed bombs, our mission goes far beyond that. We’re deeply committed to helping restore monarch butterfly populations across North America, and every planting truly makes a difference.
We’ll gladly send you a free pack of our cold-stratified milkweed seeds , so you can try again with the best possible conditions.
 

 Simply reply to this email to confirm your shipping address, and we’ll handle the rest.
 

 Thank you for being part of this journey with us. Together, we’re helping bring the monarchs back
 

 Warmly,
 __
 Hari 
 

 Lasclay
